title: Register the study capability in the CLI so Athena can run it
summary: Wire the existing athena-cap-study crate into the athena binary so the reader can pick `study` and the core can run it, with the dependency edge documented and tested. Starting the firstmate M1 study itself is not part of this change: the design says containment, the run step, and the Pages design are unbuilt and the study is a separate job.

defaults_applied.how: One focused change: register the capability. The firstmate study is deferred to its own job.
Adds a registration test, and cargo test and clippy must pass.
The dependency edge is enforced by the existing xtask policy test, so architecture.md must match.
Recovered from the repo that the crate exists and is unregistered, so the request reduces to wiring.
The design (docs/design/study-capability-m1.md) is the source. The Pages design it requires is not built here.
Docs and comments are updated so an outsider sees the capability is registered.

assumptions: `make study a capability Athena can run` means registering the existing `athena-cap-study` crate in `athena-cli`'s `capabilities()`. The crate and its `Capability` impl already exist but are not registered (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs header; wiring.rs lists only Change).

`start firstmate M1` is a separate later job: it needs a pin, containment, the run step and the Pages design, none of which exist (docs/design/study-capability-m1.md §8), and it must make no unreviewed claims about firstmate.

No `[capabilities.study]` section is added to athena.toml in this change. The study capability then runs with no configured checks or commands, as its own test expects; adding one is a governance change left for a later job.
The dependency edge cli -> cap-study must be mirrored in docs/architecture.md, because xtask/tests/policy.rs checks the documented edges.
question: Do you want the firstmate M1 study started as a separate job after this lands? I read "start firstmate M1" as that follow-up, since the design says the run step, containment and Pages are unbuilt and the pin happens at study time.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml depends on `athena-cap-study.workspace = true`, and Cargo.lock reflects the new edge.

docs/architecture.md lists `athena-cap-study` among athena-cli's dependencies and no longer says the crate is 'Not yet registered in the CLI'. The crate doc comment in athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs and the Partly built note in the design doc are updated to match.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying the study capability is registered, and docs/decisions.md records the call only if it differs from D64/D65.
A test in athena-cli asserts that the registered capability ids include `change` and `study`, with no duplicates.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, or other governance files, and nothing about firstmate is claimed or started.
Run `cargo test` (including xtask policy tests): all pass, including the architecture dependency-edge check.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.

out_of_scope: Running or reading firstmate, pinning a SHA, or any claim about firstmate
Containment, the run step, replay, and Pages publishing
Extending the Capability trait for multi-step jobs
departures: Reading acceptance is lower than the reference because 'start firstmate M1' is deferred, which the user may not want. The change is small and mechanical, so verification passes slightly more often.
